articles.title: Career turning point: “I loved the idea of staying home”: How Caitlin Clark’s decision to choose Iowa over Notre Dame changed her basketball career
articles.summary: International Sports News: Before Caitlin Clark became one of the biggest names in women’s basketball, she was a highly recruited teenager from West Des Moines, Iowa, facing a m.
articles.body: Before Caitlin Clark became one of the biggest names in women’s basketball, she was a highly recruited teenager from West Des Moines, Iowa, facing a major college decision. Notre Dame had the tradition and championships, while Iowa offered something more personal: home and the chance to help build something special.On Nov. 12, 2019, Clark committed to Iowa over Notre Dame and Iowa State. What looked like a major recruiting win for Lisa Bluder became much more than that. It became a career turning point, putting Clark on the path to becoming the NCAA’s all-time leading scorer and leading Iowa to two national championship games. ESPN later revealed just how close she came to choosing a different path.How Caitlin Clark nearly chose Notre Dame before changing her mind?Caitlin Clark’s recruitment was already unusual because some of the biggest programs in the country wanted her long before she reached college. ESPN reported in November 2019 that Clark was ranked No. 4 nationally in the 2020 recruiting class, making her the highest-ranked recruit in Iowa’s class at the time. Her final choices eventually came down to Iowa, Iowa State and Notre Dame.Notre Dame had an obvious advantage in the eyes of many people around Clark. The Fighting Irish had won the 2018 national championship under Muffet McGraw and returned to the national championship game in 2019. Clark had grown up watching Notre Dame and was particularly drawn to stars such as Skylar Diggins. ESPN’s Wright Thompson later reported that Clark’s family also wanted her to attend Notre Dame.“My family wanted me to go to Notre Dame,” Clark told ESPN. “At the end of the day they were like, you make the decision for yourself. But it’s NOTRE DAME! ‘Rudy’ was one of my favorite movies. How could you not pick Notre Dame?”The decision became even more complicated because Clark actually told McGraw that she intended to attend Notre Dame. ESPN reported that Clark called McGraw after deciding that Notre Dame was the “smart” choice. She then called Bluder to deliver the bad news while Bluder was attending a field hockey game.But the story did not end there. Clark continued to have doubts, and Iowa assistant Jan Jensen eventually reached out to see where her head was. Clark admitted that she had changed her mind. The next step was far more difficult because she had to call McGraw again and tell her she was no longer coming to Notre Dame.ESPN’s account of the recruitment showed just how emotional that moment was for Clark. She was only 17 years old, sitting in her bedroom and preparing to call one of the most respected coaches in women’s basketball. Eventually, she made the call and then contacted Bluder. Clark committed to Iowa, and the coaching staff celebrated immediately.The decision became official when Clark announced her Iowa commitment publicly. ESPN reported that she chose the Hawkeyes over Notre Dame and Iowa State, giving Bluder the highest-ranked recruit of her tenure at that point.Why Caitlin Clark’s decision to choose Iowa became the real career turning point?The importance of Caitlin Clark’s decision was not simply that she stayed close to home. It was that she chose a program where she believed she could help create something bigger.In her 2026 appearance on “Post Moves with Candace Parker and Aliyah Boston,” Clark explained the thinking behind the decision in greater detail. She said there was something about Notre Dame that ultimately did not feel right, even though she respected the program and its history.“I loved the idea of going to a school that obviously had been to the Final Four in 1992 or 1993,” Clark said during the podcast. She then explained why Iowa appealed to her so strongly: “I loved the idea of, like, staying home and, like, trying to take a place that meant a lot to me and, like, the state of Iowa to somewhere they hadn’t been in a really long time.”But staying home was only part of the reason. Clark later revealed that Bluder’s belief in her played a major role in the decision.“I think just her belief in me from Day 1 when I stepped on campus, like she gave me the keys to the offense, really the program and had always constant belief in what I could do and what I can help achieve,” Clark said, according to Basketball Network.Clark also had a clear goal from the beginning. She said that when she first committed to Iowa, she wanted to take the Hawkeyes to the Final Four. At the time, that sounded ambitious because Iowa had not reached the Final Four since 1993.“A lot of people were like that would never happen,” Clark recalled.That belief eventually became reality. Iowa reached the Final Four in Clark’s junior season and returned the following year, giving the program back-to-back Final Four appearances for the first time in its history.How Caitlin Clark turned the Iowa decision into a historic college career?Caitlin Clark did not need several years to prove that Iowa had landed a special player. She arrived in Iowa City in 2020 and quickly became the centerpiece of the Hawkeyes’ offense, eventually turning the program into a national attraction.During her four-year Iowa career, Clark averaged 28.4 points, 8.2 assists and 7.1 rebounds while playing in all 139 games. She led the Hawkeyes to their first national championship game in 2023 and returned them to the title game again in 2024.The biggest transformation came during those final two seasons. Iowa entered the 2022-23 season without a Final Four appearance since 1993. Clark then helped the Hawkeyes reach the national semifinals, where they stunned undefeated defending champion South Carolina before falling to LSU in the championship game.A year later, Iowa reached the title game again. This time, the Hawkeyes defeated LSU in the Elite Eight before losing to South Carolina in the championship game.Clark’s individual numbers eventually became almost impossible to separate from Iowa’s rise. She passed Pete Maravich to become the NCAA’s all-time leading scorer during the 2023-24 season, while the Hawkeyes became one of the biggest attractions in women’s college basketball.Yet Clark also changed as a player during those four years. She later admitted that trusting her teammates was something she had to learn.“I think that was like a process of learning over the course of my career, especially trusting my teammates,” Clark said. “I felt like I always had to do it all myself.”By her junior and senior seasons, she understood that the Hawkeyes were better when everyone around her had the freedom to flourish.“I think especially my junior and senior year, like, that was the reason why we were so good, is cuz my teammates flourished in their roles, but I also trusted them and they trusted me,” Clark added.That development helps explain why Bluder’s early belief in Clark was so important.None of that was guaranteed when Clark was sitting in her bedroom at 17, preparing to call McGraw and reverse her Notre Dame commitment.She could have chosen the established powerhouse. Instead, she chose the place where she believed she could build something.That decision eventually gave Clark four years in an Iowa program where she became the central figure, broke records and helped take the Hawkeyes to places they had not reached in decades.“I loved the idea of staying home,” Clark explained years later.For Clark, though, staying home became much bigger than geography. Iowa gave her the opportunity to play with the freedom and responsibility she wanted, while Bluder’s belief gave her the confidence to chase a goal that seemed unrealistic at the time.She did not know exactly how far that decision would take her. But she knew she wanted to build something in Iowa. Looking back at everything that followed, the choice to turn down Notre Dame and stay home stands out as one of the defining turning points of Caitlin Clark’s career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Christian McCaffrey's workload will worry many, but Kaelon Black's usage is what the 49ers and fantasy managers need
articles.summary: Matt Harmon explains why Christian McCaffrey's reduced workload is actually a good thing for the veteran RB this season.
articles.body:
I regret to inform you that I think San Francisco 49ers rookie running back Kaelon Black seeing the exact usage that we witnessed on Thursday night is smart and ideal for everyone involved.

There is no doubt that Christian McCaffrey has been a transformative player for the 49ers since he arrived midway through the 2022 NFL season. His ability to bring every rushing concept to the table, alignment versatility as a receiver and overall gravity as a player has brought the offense to life. You can feel how much Kyle Shanahan appreciates his mere presence. You can also feel his pure addiction to just smashing the McCaffrey button over and over, with a complete inability to resist playing him on nearly every snap.

It was never more apparent than last season, when McCaffrey had an abnormal workload for a running back in the modern era.

While McCaffrey was a fantasy monster once again thanks to his receiving profile, we can be honest that it clearly took a toll on him as a rusher. McCaffrey ranked 23rd among 33 running backs with over 150 carries in EPA per rush and 28th in yards after contact per rush. Just 8.7% of his carries went for 10-plus yards, 28th out of 33 backs. He was far from one of the most impactful or effective rushers last year, to be kind.

I will never get it out of my head that McCaffrey described the 2025 campaign as "the hardest year of his life." While it wasn't all about the workload or even football, it was still a strenuous season on his body. It would make all the sense in the world for the team not to grind him into the dust on a weekly basis as he enters his age-30 season.

As a matter of fact, Shanahan even said himself back in May that it would be smart to not do so again.

It was fair to be skeptical that Shanahan would follow through on his statements, considering he's behaved as a man unable to resist the McCaffrey temptation in the past. That doesn't change the fact that it was a perfectly logical desire and even a sharp move.

I can also understand any skepticism over the idea that Shanahan and the 49ers would actually trust and use a rookie running back they took in the mid-rounds. Especially because Kaelon Black was a surprise Round 3 selection who some evaluators didn't even give a draftable grade. However, his on-field profile quietly fit the exact back they needed alongside McCaffrey. In my guy James Koh's charting of Black's college film, while he didn't find him to be an exciting playmaker whatsoever, he described him "as a viable, workmanlike back" and noted "when you go through the charting, all he does is give you positive plays."

Black looked like that exact player on Thursday night: finding holes in outside zone concepts, getting what was blocked to the tune of 14 carries for 65 yards. The 49ers have needed that exact back to be able to take the grinder carries away from McCaffrey. I remember doing shows with Austin Ekeler years ago and he was constantly pleading for the Chargers to find a back like that to pass off some of the work to stay fresh. There's no doubt McCaffrey wants the same at this stage of his career and Shanahan confirmed it was his desire as well.

To the point that it's good for McCaffrey, we referenced the 2025 rushing stats, or lack thereof, earlier. In Week 1, McCaffrey took 20% of his carries for 10-plus yards and averaged 6.8 yards per carry. He looked noticeably more explosive and ran with more aggression on fewer opportunities. McCaffrey also maintained a clear lead in the passing game with 18 routes and a team-high eight targets to 10 and one for Black.

McCaffrey might not have the absolutely legendary fantasy upside we've seen in his league-winner years if this split continues — which it should. Yet, the risk of injuries and a decline in rushing efficiency are much lower as a result. I don't know about you, but I want McCaffrey here for a long time this season, not just a good time early in the year. I'll take the trade-off.

From a brass-tacks perspective, the end results here aren't even bad in fantasy. Are you going to turn your nose up at 18 opportunities and 88 yards from scrimmage? I don't think so. People already have way bigger problems with some other fantasy players and we're not even out of the opening slate. This development won't come close to one of the things I'm panicking about most from Week 1.

If we redrafted today, McCaffrey would still be a fringe Round 1 selection for me. With games against the Dolphins and Cardinals on deck the next two weeks, I can't see myself ranking him outside of the top-five running backs.

Meanwhile, Black becomes one of the best running back stashes and backup insurance policy holds in the game with perhaps some level of standalone value. By the way, to speak to the foreseeable nature of where we are, this was true before Week 1. I added him to the end of my top-150 rankings this draft season after he enjoyed a strong preseason and earned the RB2 gig. Either way, Black should be one of the most-added players heading into Week 2.

articles.title: Lindblad crashes as Antonelli fastest in Madrid
articles.summary: Arvid Lindblad crashes his Racing Bulls in Friday practice at the Spanish Grand Prix, where Kimi Antonelli sets the fastest time.
articles.body:
British rookie Arvid Lindblad crashed his Racing Bulls in Friday practice at the Spanish Grand Prix shortly after setting an impressive fourth fastest time.

The 19-year-old lost control into Turn 13, and slid sideways into the wall, damaging his front and rear suspension and breaking his front wing.

Lindblad ended the session fourth fastest, just 0.228 seconds behind pace-setter Kimi Antonelli's Mercedes in Madrid.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were second and third fastest, just over 0.1secs behind Antonelli.

Antonelli's team-mate George Russell, who trails the Italian by 66 points in the championship, was fifth fastest ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen and McLaren's Oscar Piastri.

World champion Lando Norris did not set a time in his McLaren because of a gearbox problem.

Lindblad's incident was the only one of the day in Formula 1 running, but it did back up some remarks from Russell before the first session that the new Madring track had "less margin than Monaco, purely because of the speed".

Russell added: "In Monaco, the walls are closer, but because you're going far slower, if you make a mistake, you're not into the wall as quickly, and you can recover it sometimes, a small lock-up.

"There's a lot of really fast corners, but the barrier is kind of like coming back on to the track. So, if you are to go wide and hit the wall, you're not hitting it kind of at the same angle as the car is going. The wall is sort of coming in at you."

Russell singled out Turns Five, Seven and 17, where Leclerc went off into the run-off area at Turn 17.

Russell said: "Another element of the challenge here, which probably won't cause major crashes, but I think there'll be a lot of lock-ups.

"You've got three corners where you're turning and braking, and if you lock up, the wall is right in front of you, which is very reminiscent of the corner in Baku, Turn 15. You know, the one down the hill where a lot of people go off."

There is also a section of high-speed swerves, Russell said, which is similar to the fast Jeddah street track in Saudi Arabia.
authors: Andrew Benson - F1 Correspondent in Madrid

articles.title: Borussia Dortmund’s Konstantinos Karetsas discharged from hospital, yet still out for Paderborn
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund will be without Konstantinos Karetsas for Saturday’s Bundesliga home fixture against SC Paderborn as further examinations continue followin...
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund will be without Konstantinos Karetsas for Saturday's Bundesliga home fixture against SC Paderborn as further examinations continue following the 18-year-old's worrying withdrawal from Tuesday's Champions League victory over Villarreal . Karetsas has since been released from hospital after suffering circulatory problems during Dortmund's 3-2 win at the Westfalenstadion.

The Greek international did not participate in team training on Thursday and will not be available for the weekend. Dortmund sporting director Ole Book has now confirmed that initial examinations have yet to establish a specific cause.

"He is doing as well as can be expected under the circumstances," Book told the local Ruhr Nachrichten newspaper. "Further examinations are ongoing. We want to get to the bottom of this properly. The prognosis will then depend on that."

Book emphasized that Karetsas' health remains the club's overriding concern.

While Karetsas' mother Irena Kitsinis told Belgian newspaper Het Nieuwsblad that the episode appeared to have been related to dehydration, Dortmund have not yet established a definitive explanation for the problem.

The youngster has consequently been ruled out of the Paderborn fixture, with no timetable currently available for his return.

Dortmund remain cautious over Karetsas return

Karetsas' withdrawal against Villarreal caused considerable concern among his teammates and club officials. The summer signing sat down on the pitch during the first half before eventually being carried off on a stretcher. Dortmund subsequently confirmed that he had complained of circulatory problems before being transported to hospital.

Managing director Lars Ricken later praised the squad's response to seeing a teammate leave the pitch under uncertain circumstances, while Book acknowledged immediately after the match that the incident had caused concern throughout the club.

Karetsas has since been discharged, providing Dortmund with some positive news, but the club have made clear that no return will be contemplated until the cause of the episode has been properly investigated.

Head coach Niko Kovac confirmed ahead of Saturday's match that Karetsas will not feature against Paderborn.

His absence further reduces Dortmund's options in the advanced midfield positions after fellow Greek international Giannis Konstantelias suffered a major ACL tear in the opening Bundesliga victory over Hamburger SV .

Ethan Nwaneri , who replaced Karetsas against Villarreal, impressed after coming on and represents one of the alternatives available to Kovac this weekend.

articles.title: Drew Brees thinks Bears Caleb Williams is closer to a breakthrough than you think
articles.summary: Count Drew Brees among those who see big things on the horizon for the Bears QB1, Caleb Williams. @kdthompson5 has the details here.
articles.body:
For all Caleb Williams ' brilliance in his third season with the Chicago Bears , the burgeoning star quarterback can still get that much better as a passer—a frightening prospect for the NFL, if you ask me.

In particular, Williams' 58.1% completion percentage, a year after completing just 62.5% of his passes as a rookie, is due for an improvement in Year 3, which will mark his second under Ben Johnson.

But for those worried about whether Williams can make meaningful strides in that area, Hall-of-Fame quarterback Drew Brees had some advice for Williams that might put things in perspective.

Brees, who is now working as a color analyst for FOX Sports alongside Adam Amin, recently spoke with Williams as part of their preparations for the Bears' season-opening contest against the Carolina Panthers . Amin shared an especially interesting piece of that conversation on 104.3 The Score yesterday . (Also, don't forget to check out Adam's chat with our own Bill Zimmerman when you're done reading this.)

"Drew's line at the end of our conversation with Caleb—he said, 'You know what the difference is between a 60% passer and a 70% passer?' Caleb's answer was—he was hesitant, but he goes, 'Is it checkdowns?'

"Drew's answer was 'Three completions.'" You get three more completions per game when you're probably going to throw the ball 30 times per game."

First of all, Williams getting to speak with one of the greatest quarterbacks to ever do it—a man who completed almost 68% of his career pass attempts—is absolutely invaluable.

Secondly, what a way to put the task at hand in plain but attainable terms.

When you take away the league-leading 40 throwaways Williams made last year—another underrated sign of his growth—you could generally point to two or three passes a game where the ball simply got away from the young quarterback, who had the third-highest "bad-throw" percentage among all quarterbacks according to Pro Football Reference. (Plus, let's not forget he also suffered from the fourth-highest drop rate from his pass catchers at 5.5%. He also had 18 balls batted at the line of scrimmage, second-most in the NFL.)

The good news, Amin said, is that these improvements are a matter of smaller adjustments and fundamental tweaks than wholesale overhauls.

"A few adjustments here and there are all it's going to take to get small plays that lead to extended drives that lead to four extra points instead of having to settle for a field goal. These are the little things that build up and compound over time, and that's a good entry point to be in Year 2 in an offense," the broadcaster said.

A little bit of positive regression in each of these stats, and it wouldn't be hard to see Williams' completion rate jump into the mid-60s, even as he continues to big-game hunt and generate explosive plays.

We might be talking about an MVP-caliber player sooner rather than later.

And all it might take, at least to start with, is three more completions a game. Imagine that.

articles.title: Athletic Club forward Williams retires from Ghana duty
articles.summary: Inaki Williams says the time has come to bring his journey with the Black Stars to an end four years after making his international debut.
articles.body:
Athletic Club forward Inaki Williams has announced his retirement from international duty with Ghana .

The 32-year-old scored two goals in 28 caps for the Black Stars after making his debut in September 2022.

He featured for the West Africans at the 2022 and 2026 Fifa World Cups and the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon).

Williams appeared twice at this year's World Cup as Ghana were knocked out in the last 32 by Colombia .

"I feel the time has come to bring my journey with the Ghana national team to an end," he said in a post on social media.

"I leave happy, proud and with the peace of mind of knowing that I gave everything every time I wore this shirt."

Williams, who was born in Bilbao to Ghanaian parents, chose to represent the Black Stars after previously playing for Spain at youth level and in a 2016 friendly at senior level.

His younger brother Nico, who also plays for Athletic Club in Bilbao, chose to represent Spain and has gone on to become a World Cup and European Championship winner with La Roja.

Inaki Williams' announcement comes a week after it was confirmed that Carlos Queiroz would return as Ghana coach in the build-up to the 2027 Afcon in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

He said his time with Ghana had given him "much more than football".

"It has allowed me to come back home, feel even closer to my roots and experience the enormous pride of representing my country and wearing this flag on my chest," he added.

"Thank you from the bottom of my heart to everyone who has been part of this journey and for all the love you have always shown me.

"Ghana will always be a part of me. I will continue supporting the Black Stars as one of you, wherever I am."

articles.title: Rudy Gobert Gets A Major Respect Nod From Nikola Jokic
articles.summary: Rudy Gobert has spent years dealing with mixed reviews about his defense. That debate looks different when one of the NBA’s best offensive players gives him...
articles.body:
Rudy Gobert has spent years dealing with mixed reviews about his defense. That debate looks different when one of the NBA's best offensive players gives him credit for making the game harder.

Nikola Jokic has faced Gobert plenty of times and knows where the Timberwolves center can cause problems. His latest comments give Gobert a notable endorsement from someone who has spent years trying to attack him.

Rudy Gobert Earned Nikola Jokic's Respect

Jokic discussed the defenders who make his job difficult during an appearance on the Jao Mile podcast . When the conversation reached Gobert, the Denver star dismissed the idea that the Timberwolves center is overrated on defense.

"Rudy Gobert, I know people have all kinds of opinions about him, but Rudy is a good defender. He showed it in the last playoffs," Jokic said.

This praise means a lot , especially since Jokic still puts up big numbers against Gobert. Jokic isn't saying he can completely shut him down, but he is admitting that Gobert forces him to earn every single bucket.

The 2026 playoffs gave Jokic a fresh look at that challenge. Minnesota trusted Gobert to defend him without constant double teams, allowing the Timberwolves to keep their other defenders focused on Denver's shooters. The Wolves eventually eliminated the Nuggets in six games.

Gobert's biggest impact came when Minnesota stopped trying to hide the matchup. He took on Jokic directly and used his size to contest drives, absorb contact and challenge shots around the basket.

In Game 2, Jokic went 1-for-8 from the field when Gobert was his primary defender. He still finished with 24 points, 15 rebounds and 8 assists, showing why defending him is about limiting his comfort rather than expecting a complete shutdown.

That defensive approach also helped the Timberwolves protect the rest of the floor. Gobert could stay attached to Jokic while Minnesota's perimeter defenders stayed closer to Denver's shooters.

Jokic acknowledged that challenge again when discussing Gobert's work in the postseason. His praise came after a series in which Minnesota repeatedly trusted its center to handle one of the hardest defensive assignments in basketball.

Rudy Gobert Has A Different Kind Of Endorsement

Gobert has won four Defensive Player of the Year awards, but his playoff defense has remained a frequent topic of debate. That makes Jokic's comments especially useful because they come from the player who has had to solve that defense himself.

The Denver-Minnesota series did not turn Gobert into an unbeatable defender. Jokic averaged 25.8 points, 13.2 rebounds and 9.5 assists across the six games.

It did show what Gobert can do when Minnesota allows him to play to his strengths. He can occupy Jokic without constant help, giving his teammates the freedom to handle other threats.

That may be why Jokic's praise stands out. Gobert does not need to erase an offensive superstar from the box score to prove his value. Making that superstar work harder is part of the job, and Jokic has now said plainly that Gobert does it well.

articles.title: Texas football news: The Arch Manning skill that has Ohio State worried about getting 'killed'
articles.summary: The Saturday showdown between No. 4 Texas and No. 1 Ohio State has much more at stake than a win or loss. For Texas QB Arch Manning, it’s proving he’s NFL ma...
articles.body:
The Saturday showdown between No. 4 Texas and No. 1 Ohio State has much more at stake than a win or loss. For Texas QB Arch Manning , it's proving he's NFL material.

Ironically, nobody recognizes that more than the Buckeyes themselves.

On Friday, Ohio State coaches revealed the skills Manning brings to the field that they plan to watch for, per Bruce Feldman of The Athletic.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

One defensive coach talked about the difference between him on film and how he was last year.

"He's fixed his throwing mechanics" he said.

Last year, Manning completed 17 out of 30 passes against Ohio in a 14-7 loss. He added one touchdown and threw one interception. The Ohio State defense stopped him in his tracks.

Additionally, a source close to the Longhorns revealed to The Athletic a critical update about Manning.

"He's cleaner — and he's way more confident now," the source said. "There's more talent around him. He was the team's best running threat last year."

But a source with the Buckeyes emphasized the one thing that could "kill" them.

"His legs will kill you if you let him out" he said.

Texas got the season started in the right way, a blowout 59-7 loss over Texas State last weekend. Ohio State steamrolled past Ball State 56-3.

Last season, Manning finished the season with 3,163 passing yards and 26 touchdowns. Against Texas State, he threw for 305 yards and 4 touchdowns.

He is highly regarded as a top draft prospect heading into 2027. Some are considering him as the possible No.1 pick in the Draft.

In five games, Ohio State holds the edge over Texas 3-2.
